summary:
Bahrain Trend Detective is an interactive website that uses over 30 years of NASA satellite data to track two vital signs for Bahrain: rising sea levels and rising water temperatures. It combines NASA-SSH and MEaSUREs sea surface height, MODIS sea surface temperature (2003–2026) and GEBCO bathymetry, with trends tested for statistical significance.

Temperature: the waters around Bahrain are warming about 0.70 °C per decade. A bathymetry-downscaled model estimates that shallow bays such as Tubli Bay reach 35.4 °C in summer, 2.2 °C hotter than the open Gulf.

Sea level: the sea is rising about 4.2 mm per year, roughly 14 cm since 1992, a statistically significant trend.

Users can play an animated map to watch the change year by year and explore six coastal zones. Public Awareness mode explains impacts on coral, fisheries, drainage and desalination in everyday language. Research & Crisis Command mode offers detailed charts and a compound flood simulator up to 2100.

Bahrain is a low-lying island in one of Earth’s hottest seas, so turning space data into local action helps protect its people, coasts and ecosystems.
details:
Bahrain sea detective is a data repository of gathered public NASA research data that allows the reader to view Nasa's raw data in a more user-friendly manner. It operates by gathering Nasa's raw data using two specialized python scripts that allows the user to convert thousands of raw data files into readable csv files that are ready for use. Then the csv files are used to create visual graphs, which are used to make people understand the situation better.

It is unique compared to more generalized earth data repository as it features an auto-pilot summary (limited to 4 chapters as of now) a simulator which features Bahrain's main coastal towns/cities and how varying conditions may affect them, it has 2 "modes" one tab is for a more general and simplified overview of the data, offering surface level information but not ignoring the criticality of it, this is for the benefit of those inexperienced with data and Earth data information.

Our project, the Bahrain Sea detective's intended goal and impact is the long-term awareness and action of the slow disaster of climate change and its damage on islands similar to our Bahrain. It is meant to take the critical raw and unreadable information from Nasa and convert it into a format people can understand and comprehend. As for the tools, coding languages, hardware, and software our team have used, we made use of python with the assist of generative AI, HTML for the coding of the website and CSS styling for the design of the website which we did use AI for help with the general layout and design, finally, we used GitHub in order to create the link for the repository and share it with others.

Regarding the project's creativity we have added features that are not commonly found among popular data sites, those being a interactive thermal map, and the 2 modes of "Public Awareness and "Research and crisis command".

Furthermore, we also have added a simulator as previously mentioned, as well as the satellites we have used in the process of our research and lastly, an opensource version of the python script used for the data collection process.

As for the considerations of the team, there are the types of data we could discuss, Questions such as: "what would seasoned scientists learn from our website in which they can't in normal data repositories?", the data inconsistency as Bahrain is not recorded as an individual entity in NASA so statistical techniques such as the Mann-Kendall test and Sen's slope, were used to keep the data as accurate as possible.
